actions.label: Request host/client MWB diagnostics
actions.note: Ask for the synchronized host/client evidence needed to triage the asymmetric MWB visibility failure.

comment.body:
Thanks for the detailed three-machine description — the red-border transition on the host is especially useful. To move this beyond a general “MWB does not work” report, please provide the following:

1. **Fresh diagnostics from both sides** — Please reproduce the problem, then immediately comment `/bugreport` from the **host** and from **one affected client** so both ZIPs capture the same failure window.
2. **Version matrix** — Please list the exact PowerToys version on the desktop and both laptops.
3. **Connection confirmation** — Please confirm whether all three machines are using the same security key and whether any VPN, guest network, or subnet boundary is involved.

That host/client evidence pair is what the MWB team needs to separate a discovery/handshake failure from a matrix UI/state problem.

issue_context.summary: In a three-machine Mouse Without Borders setup, clients can see the host but the host cannot keep the clients visible and remote borders fall back to red after a short refresh.
known_information: The original issue is on 0.100.2 from the Microsoft Store.
A commenter describes a reproducible three-machine configuration with the host seeing only itself while both clients see all three machines.
The same commenter says the behavior persists across restart, reinstall, and both line/grid layouts.
No diagnostics bundle or exact per-machine version list is attached.
inferences: The asymmetry suggests a host-side state-sync or handshake issue, but the current report is not specific enough to distinguish connection state from UI-matrix persistence.
Because the borders flip from blue back to red after refresh, time-correlated logs from both host and client matter more than another textual paraphrase.
issue_context.analysis: This is a good candidate for a targeted diagnostic request. The report is concrete enough to know what to ask for, but not yet concrete enough for a fix plan.
initial_investigation: Re-read the original body and the detailed follow-up comment.
Confirmed the issue still lacks any bug report ZIP, version matrix, or current MWB state dump.
Compared the symptom to other MWB issues in this batch and kept it separate from the InvalidKey/mixed-version pairing report.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostics bundle from the host and from one affected client immediately after the host falls back to red borders.
information_gaps.why_needed: The host/client log pair is needed to see whether the failure is handshake, discovery, or matrix-state sync.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please reproduce the problem, then immediately comment `/bugreport` from the host and from one affected client so both ZIPs capture the same failure window.

information_gaps.information: The exact PowerToys version on all three machines.
information_gaps.why_needed: Version skew is a known confounder in MWB pairing problems and needs to be ruled out first.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please list the PowerToys version shown in About on the desktop and both laptops.

information_gaps.information: Whether all three machines use the same security key and whether VPN or subnet boundaries are involved.
information_gaps.why_needed: That helps separate matrix-UI problems from connectivity/pairing state problems.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Please confirm whether all machines are using the same security key and whether any VPN, guest network, or subnet separation is involved while reproducing.

judgment.rationale: The topology description is useful, but the current report still lacks the host/client diagnostics needed to tell whether the red-border host visibility problem is discovery, state sync, or security-key state.
evidence: The original issue only says the feature does not work even when rerun as administrator.
A follow-up commenter adds a concrete three-machine scenario where clients see the host, but the host sees only itself and remote borders turn red again after refresh.
No bug report ZIP, version matrix, or network-context evidence is attached.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for one host/client diagnostic pair plus the exact version matrix so the MWB team can classify the red-border failure mode.

fix_assessment.rationale: The report is real but not yet specific enough to isolate whether the failing layer is discovery, sync, pairing, or UI state.
